question: What is the angle of elevation of the sun when the shadow of a pole is √3 times the length of the pole?
solution:
**Given:**

The shadow of a pole is √3 times the length of the pole.

**Concept used:**

tanθ = Perpendicular/base

tan 30° = (1)/({sqrt 3)}

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/770699d6d8aa29da53022d6e8f873eaf1e967d8652e651f3ab2e5784aea70c92.png] 

The height of the tower be h.

So, the height of the shadow be √3h

Now, In ΔABC,

⇒ tan ∠ACB = (h)/({sqrt 3h)}

⇒ tan ∠ACB = (1)/({sqrt 3)}

⇒ tan ∠ACB = tan 30° 

⇒ ∠ACB = 30° 

**∴ The angle of elevation is 30° **
